claim: The General Assembly convenes each year on the second Wednesday of January and is a continuous body
quote: The General Assembly shall convene each year on the second Wednesday of January.

claim: A bill passed after May 31 cannot take effect before the next June 1 without a three-fifths vote
quote: A bill passed after May 31 shall not become effective prior to June 1 of the next calendar year

claim: A bill passed before June 1 with no effective date takes effect January 1 of the following year
quote: shall become effective on January 1 of the following year, or upon its becoming a law, whichever is later

claim: The Governor has 60 calendar days after presentment to act on a bill
quote: Any bill not so returned by the Governor within 60 calendar days after it is presented to him shall become law.

claim: Bills must be presented to the Governor within 30 days of passage
quote: shall be presented to the Governor within 30 calendar days after its passage

claim: Even years: general election the first Tuesday after the first Monday of November; general primary the third Tuesday in March
quote: an election to be known as the general primary election shall be held on the third Tuesday in March

claim: Odd years: consolidated election the first Tuesday in April; consolidated primary the last Tuesday in February
quote: consolidated election shall be held on the first Tuesday in April

claim: Odd years: consolidated primary the last Tuesday in February
quote: consolidated primary election shall be held on the last Tuesday in February

claim: The consolidated election moves when it conflicts with Passover
quote: that election shall be postponed to the first Tuesday following the last day of Passover

claim: County officers, including county board members, are filled at the even-year general election
quote: County elected officers, including State's Attorney, County Board member, County Commissioners, and elected President of the County Board or County Chief Executive

claim: Municipal officers are filled at the odd-year consolidated election
quote: At the consolidated election in the appropriate odd-numbered years, the following offices shall be filled: (1) Municipal officers

claim: Township officers, highway commissioners, park, library and fire protection district boards are filled at the consolidated election
quote: Township officers, including township park commissioners, township library directors

claim: Highway commissioners and road district clerks are filled at the consolidated election
quote: Highway commissioners and road district clerks

claim: School board members (outside Chicago) and community college boards are filled at the consolidated election
quote: Members of Community College district boards

claim: Elected school boards are filled at the consolidated election
quote: Elected members of school boards, school trustees, directors of boards of school directors

claim: Chicago Board of Education members are elected at the even-year general election in a nonpartisan election
quote: the election of members of the Chicago Board of Education shall be a nonpartisan election

claim: Party nominations at the consolidated primary do not apply to school, community college, fire protection and similar nonpartisan offices
quote: and except those offices listed in paragraphs (12) through (17) of subsection (c)

claim: No election may be held on a date other than the consolidated schedule, notwithstanding any municipal charter
quote: No election may be held on any date other than a date on which an election is scheduled under Section 2A-1.1

claim: The Election Code governs nominations and elections notwithstanding any other statute or municipal charter
quote: notwithstanding the provisions of any other statute or municipal charter

claim: A municipality with annual elections may fill some offices at the even-year general primary
quote: where the municipality has provided for annual elections to elect municipal officers

claim: A voter must declare a party to vote in a primary
quote: Unless he declares his party affiliations as required by this Article.

claim: A voter states a party affiliation to the judges and receives only that party's ballot; refusal means no primary ballot
quote: No person who refuses to state his party affiliation shall be allowed to vote at a primary.

claim: Voting a party ballot at the general primary bars running as an independent at the following general election
quote: who voted the ballot of an established political party at a general primary election may not file a statement of candidacy as a candidate of a different established political party, a new political party, or as an independent candidate

claim: A voter may also vote in the primary of a party established only in a local subdivision
quote: may nonetheless also declare his affiliation with a political party established only within a political subdivision

claim: The party primary covers county and city, village and town officers, but not school elections, most township elections, park districts, special charter cities, or municipalities of 5,000 or less unless they opt in
quote: the nomination of municipal officers for cities, villages, and incorporated towns with a population of 5,000 or less

claim: School elections are outside the party primary article
quote: This Article 7 shall not apply to (i) the nomination of candidates for school elections and township elections

claim: A primary nominee is the person with the most votes (no primary runoff)
quote: The person receiving the highest number of votes at a primary as a candidate of a party for the nomination for an office shall be the candidate of that party

claim: Municipalities of under 5,000 may nominate party candidates by caucus
quote: make one nomination for each office therein to be filled at any election for officers of a municipality with a population of less than 5,000

claim: Article 4 (commission) and Article 5 (managerial) municipalities elect on a nonpartisan basis
quote: requires election to such office on a nonpartisan basis and does not permit political party nominations (including without limitation Articles 4 and 5 of the Municipal Code)

claim: Villages may elect in nonpartisan primary and general elections; villages partisan before 1992 may stay partisan; voters can switch by referendum
quote: Villages that have nominated and elected candidates for president and trustees in partisan elections prior to January 1, 1992, may continue to hold partisan elections

claim: A village can vote to stop nonpartisan elections
quote: Shall candidates for president and trustees of (name of village) no longer be elected in nonpartisan primary and general elections?

claim: A village can vote to adopt nonpartisan elections
quote: Shall candidates for president and trustees of (name of village) be elected in nonpartisan primary and general elections?

claim: Township officers in most townships are nominated by party caucus
quote: a caucus shall be held by the voters of each established political party in a township to nominate its candidates

claim: Larger townships may choose a party primary instead of a caucus
quote: determine that its candidates for township offices shall be nominated by primary in accordance with the general election law

claim: Independent candidates for local office get on the ballot by nomination papers
quote: Nominations of independent candidates for public office within any district or political subdivision less than the State, may be made by nomination papers

claim: A circulator may not circulate for more than one party, or for an independent plus a party, for the same election
quote: no person shall circulate or certify petitions for candidates of more than one political party, or for an independent candidate or candidates in addition to one political party

claim: A party primary petition signer may not sign for more than one party
quote: may not sign petitions for or be a candidate in the primary of more than one party

claim: County officers are elected by plurality
quote: to each of the persons having the highest number of votes, for the several county offices

claim: Each county elects a sheriff, clerk and treasurer, and may elect or appoint other officers; county officers serve four-year terms
quote: Each county shall elect a sheriff, county clerk and treasurer

claim: Elected county officers serve four-year terms at general elections
quote: elected county officers shall be elected for terms of four years at general elections as provided by law

claim: Every county elects a county board, with size set by ordinance within limits
quote: A county board shall be elected in each county.

claim: Township counties under 3 million set a board of 5 to 29 members, at large or by districts, at each reapportionment
quote: may consist of not less than 5 nor more than 29 members

claim: County board seats rotate through 2- and 4-year terms after each redistricting
quote: successive terms of 2 years, 4 years and 4 years

claim: A county board may let voters elect its chairman
quote: may provide that the chairman of the county board shall be elected by the voters of the county

claim: Counties not under township organization may use a three-member commission elected at large to six-year terms
quote: In every county not under township organization that is organized as a commission form of government having 3 commissioners elected at large

claim: Commissioners in such counties serve six-year terms, one elected each general election
quote: one commissioner shall be elected to serve for a term of 6 years

claim: A county with an elected chief executive, and a municipality over 25,000, is a home rule unit automatically
quote: A County which has a chief executive officer elected by the electors of the county and any municipality which has a population of more than 25,000 are home rule units.

claim: Home rule counties provide for officers only in the manner set in art. VII § 4
quote: A home rule county shall have the power to provide for its officers, their manner of selection and terms of office in the manner set forth in Section 4 of this Article.

claim: Cook County elects 17 commissioners every four years
quote: There shall be elected every 4 years by the legal voters of Cook County 17 county commissioners

claim: The President of the Cook County Board is elected at large and is the county's chief executive
quote: The President of the Cook County Board shall be elected from the County at large and shall be the chief executive officer of the County.

claim: Cook County may change how its board is elected by ordinance or referendum; other counties only by referendum
quote: No county, other than Cook County, may change its method of electing board members except as approved by county-wide referendum.

claim: Voters in a county decide by referendum whether to have township organization
quote: The General Assembly shall provide by law for the formation of townships in any county when approved by county-wide referendum.

claim: Townships elect a supervisor, clerk, assessor and collector to four-year terms
quote: there shall be elected a township supervisor. The supervisor shall be ex-officio supervisor of general assistance. The supervisor shall hold office for a term of 4 years

claim: The township board is the supervisor and four trustees elected at large
quote: the township board shall consist of the supervisor and 4 other members elected at large from the township

claim: Townships hold an annual town meeting of voters each April
quote: The annual township meeting in the respective townships for the transaction of the business of the township shall be held on the second Tuesday of April in each year

claim: Township elections follow the consolidated schedule
quote: Elections for township officers shall be held in accordance with the consolidated schedule of elections

claim: Municipalities are cities, villages and incorporated towns; school districts are not units of local government
quote: "Municipalities" means cities, villages and incorporated towns.

claim: Cities elect a mayor, alderpersons, a clerk and a treasurer (treasurer may be appointed under 10,000); villages and incorporated towns elect a president, trustees and a clerk
quote: In all villages and incorporated towns, there shall be elected a president, trustees, and a clerk

claim: Cities elect a mayor, alderpersons, a city clerk and a city treasurer
quote: there shall be elected a mayor, alderpersons, a city clerk, and a city treasurer

claim: A village president may also be called mayor; the chief executive serves four years unless a two-year term was adopted
quote: The chief executive officer of a village shall be a village president, who may also be called a mayor.

claim: Municipal chief executives serve 4-year terms by default
quote: The chief executive officer shall hold office for 4 years

claim: Villages elect six trustees to four-year terms
quote: the electors of the village shall elect 6 trustees. The term of office of the trustees shall be 4 years

claim: Villages under 5,000 can cut the board to four trustees by referendum
quote: whether the board of trustees shall be comprised of 4 members rather than 6 members

claim: The number of alderpersons in a city is set by population brackets
quote: in cities not exceeding 3,000 inhabitants, 6 alderpersons

claim: Cities have half as many wards as alderpersons (two per ward by default)
quote: every city shall have one-half as many wards as the total number of alderpersons to which the city is entitled

claim: Cities under 100,000 can halve the council to one alderperson per ward by referendum
quote: a proposition to restrict the number of alderpersons to one-half of the total authorized by Section 3.1-20-10, with one alderperson representing each ward

claim: Municipalities under 500,000 can cut terms from four years to two by referendum
quote: a proposition to reduce the terms of the elective officers of the municipality from 4 years to 2 years

claim: A village or town of 2,500 or more may choose to become a city; class does not change automatically with population
quote: Any incorporated town or village having a population of not less than 2,500 persons including 2,000 living in immobile dwellings, may incorporate as a city

claim: A municipality over 25,000 is home rule automatically; smaller ones may become home rule by referendum; any may opt out by referendum
quote: Other municipalities may elect by referendum to become home rule units.

claim: A home rule unit may vote by referendum not to be home rule
quote: A home rule unit by referendum may elect not to be a home rule unit.

claim: A home rule municipality may change its officers, their selection and terms only by referendum or as authorized by law
quote: A home rule municipality shall have the power to provide for its officers, their manner of selection and terms of office only as approved by referendum or as otherwise authorized by law.

claim: Non-home-rule municipalities may change their officers and form of government by referendum
quote: in the case of municipalities, to provide by referendum for their officers, manner of selection and terms of office

claim: A form-of-government ordinance under art. VII § 7 may provide for runoff elections
quote: such offices shall be filled by election or by runoff election as may be provided by such ordinance

claim: Townships, school districts and special districts have only powers granted by law
quote: Townships, school districts, special districts and units, designated by law as units of local government, which exercise limited governmental powers or powers in respect to limited governmental subjects shall have only powers granted by law.

claim: Most school districts of 1,000 to 500,000 are governed by a seven-member board of education with four-year terms
quote: shall be governed by a board of education consisting of 7 members

claim: The Chicago mayor is elected in a nonpartisan election; a majority at the February consolidated primary wins, otherwise a top-two runoff in April
quote: The candidate receiving a majority of the votes cast for mayor at the consolidated primary election shall be declared mayor.

claim: Chicago mayoral runoff is held at the consolidated election
quote: If no candidate receives a majority of the votes, a runoff election shall be held at the consolidated election

claim: Chicago mayor is elected in a nonpartisan election
quote: quadrennially thereafter in a nonpartisan election

claim: Chicago city clerk and treasurer are also elected nonpartisan with majority and runoff
quote: there shall be elected also in a nonpartisan election a city clerk and a city treasurer

claim: Chicago has 50 wards
quote: The city of Chicago shall be divided into fifty wards.

claim: One alderperson per ward, four-year terms
quote: one alderperson shall be elected from each of the 50 wards provided for by this Article

claim: An alderperson needs a majority; otherwise a supplementary (runoff) election
quote: The candidate receiving a majority of the votes cast for alderperson in each ward at any general or special election shall be declared elected.

claim: Chicago alderperson elections are held on the last Tuesday of February, with runoffs in April
quote: on the last Tuesday of February of such year

claim: Sanitary district trustees, including the Metropolitan Water Reclamation District, are elected at the November general election
quote: Trustee of the Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago, and elected Trustee of other Sanitary Districts

claim: Officers of cities and villages organized under special charters are not nominated through the party primary
quote: the nomination of officers of cities and villages organized under special charters
